title: Fertility and the vote: how fragile is the published analysis?
subtitle: Real survey data, held out. Borges starts from the published analysis and looks for the smallest change that reverses it.
question: Does the difference in voting between women at high and at low fertility on the day they filled in the questionnaire depend on relationship status, such that women in committed relationships are less likely to vote for Obama at high fertility and single women more likely (a fertility by relationship status interaction)?

decision_rule.metric: fertility by relationship status interaction on the log-odds of voting for Obama: the high minus low fertility difference among women in committed relationships minus the same difference among single women

provenance: Real data, public on OSF (Steegen et al. 2016) with the original author's permission; no licence stated
story: 502 women surveyed before the 2012 US presidential election, Study 2 of the paper behind the fertility cases. Borges is given the published analysis of the vote, as Steegen et al. reconstructed it, and asked how fragile it is. The case was added after the code it runs on was frozen, and every run of it is reported: it is a held-out test. Real data, nothing planted; a live run only.

column_notes.WorkerID: the unique identifier of a participant
column_notes.Rel1: 'How much do you believe in God?' 1-9
column_notes.Rel2: 'I see myself as a religiously oriented person.' 1-9
column_notes.Rel3: 'I believe that God or a Higher Power is responsible for my existence.' 1-9
column_notes.Marriage: 'Marriage is between a man and a woman.' 1-7 agreement
column_notes.StemCell: 'Stem cell research is moral and can be useful for science.' 1-7 agreement
column_notes.RestrictAbortion: 'Laws should restrict abortion in all or most cases.' 1-7 agreement
column_notes.FreeMarket: 'In nearly every instance, the free market allocates resources most efficiently.' 1-7 agreement
column_notes.RichTax: 'The rich should pay a higher tax rate than the middle class.' 1-7 agreement
column_notes.StLiving: 'Government should ensure that all citizens meet a certain minimum standard of living.' 1-7 agreement
column_notes.Profit: 'Business corporations make too much profit.' 1-7 agreement
column_notes.Sure1: in reference to StartDateofLastPeriod, 'How sure are you about that date?' 1-9
column_notes.Sure2: in reference to StartDateofPeriodBeforeLast, 'How sure are you about that date?' 1-9
column_notes.Relationship: answer to 'What is your current romantic relationship status?' (1) not dating/romantically involved with anyone, (2) dating or involved with only one partner, (3) engaged or living with my partner, (4) married
column_notes.ReportedCycleLength: answer to 'How many days long are your menstrual cycles? (for most women, the range is between 25-35 days) Keep in mind this is the number of days from the start of one menstrual period to the start of the next menstrual period and NOT the length of your menstrual bleeding.'; has missing values
column_notes.Vote: answer to 'Imagine walking into the voting booth today. Who would you vote for in the presidential election?' 0 = Mitt Romney (Republican), 1 = Barack Obama (Democrat)
column_notes.Donate: answer to 'For the next part of the study we will donate $1 to the presidential campaign of your preferred candidate. Please indicate which candidate's campaign you would like us to donate $1 to.' 0 = Mitt Romney, 1 = Barack Obama
column_notes.DateTesting: date the participant filled in the questionnaire
column_notes.StartDateofLastPeriod: the participant's best estimate of the date she started her last period; has missing values
column_notes.StartDateofPeriodBeforeLast: the participant's best estimate of the date she started the period before her last period; has missing values
column_notes.StartDateNext: the participant's estimate of the date her next period will start; has missing values

analysis: vote = Vote (1 = Obama); cycle length = StartDateofLastPeriod minus StartDateofPeriodBeforeLast in days; next onset = StartDateofLastPeriod plus that cycle length; cycle day = 28 minus the days from DateTesting to the next onset, set to 1 below 1 and to 28 above 28; for WorkerID 15 and 16, whose period dates are missing, the cycle day of the original authors' file, 11 and 18; high fertility = cycle days 7 to 14, low fertility = cycle days 17 to 25, rows on other days dropped; single = Relationship 1 or 2, committed = Relationship 3 or 4; no other exclusions; logistic regression of Vote on high fertility, committed and their product, with the model's own standard errors.
